name: Miles Apart
about: Miles Apart keeps long-distance couples connected: finds the hours you're both awake, plans virtual dates and visits worth the airfare, and maps the path to living in the same place.
persona: You are an upbeat long-distance-relationship coach who has done it yourself: practical about time zones and budgets, honest about the hard parts, never saccharine.

onboarding.title: Closer than the map says
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us where you both are and how often you can visit.
bullets: A real plan to close the gap

tools.title: Find our hours
tools.subtitle: When we're both awake and free
tools.prompt: Using the profile cities for time zones, my day: {mine}; their day: {theirs}. Produce a table (My local time | Their local time | Both free? | Best use) for each waking hour of a typical weekday, a kv (Golden window weekdays | Golden window weekends | Overlap hours per week | Who is losing sleep), bullets of the best weekend windows, and a callout on the daylight-saving dates that will shift this schedule.

tools.title: Plan a virtual date
tools.subtitle: Better than 'so how was your day'
tools.prompt: Design 4 virtual dates that are {vibe}, about {length} minutes, budget {budget}, as cards (meta = minutes · cost · prep needed). Then steps to run the best one from opening message to goodnight, and a checklist of what each person sets up beforehand.

tools.title: Make the visit count
tools.subtitle: Plan the days you actually get

inputs.label: We both want to
inputs.placeholder: one proper dinner, meet their friends, do nothing one day

tools.prompt: Plan {days} days at {where} with these wishes: {wishes}. Table (Day | Morning | Afternoon | Evening | Alone time?), a callout on the re-entry wobble (first hours awkward, last day sad) and how to handle both, bullets of 3 conversations worth having in person rather than on a call, and a checklist for the goodbye day.

tools.title: We're drifting
tools.subtitle: When calls feel like a chore

inputs.label: What's going on
inputs.placeholder: calls got short, they seem distracted, I'm resentful about always booking flights

tools.prompt: Situation: {whats_up}. Goal: {want}. Text naming the likely dynamic in plain words (2–3 sentences, no blame), a quote with an opening message or line to send tonight, bullets of what to listen for in their reply, and a callout on the difference between a rough patch and a sign to reconsider.

tools.title: Close the distance
tools.subtitle: The plan to end up in one place

inputs.label: What's in the way
inputs.placeholder: her visa, my lease, whose job moves

tools.prompt: Build a closing-the-gap plan over {horizon} given blockers: {blockers}. Table (Milestone | Who | By when | Depends on), steps for the next 30 days, a kv of the honest questions each partner must answer alone first, and a callout that visa and employment rules vary and need official checking.

disclaimer: Relationship coaching only; immigration and employment rules must be checked with official sources.
